items.stem: IT governance is primarily the responsibility of:

options.text: The board and executive leadership, who set direction and oversight
options.rationale: Correct: governance is a board/executive accountability for direction and oversight.
Front-line staff execute operations, they do not set governance.
Auditors provide assurance, not governance direction.
Vendors supply products; they do not govern the enterprise.

items.explanation: Correct: governance is a board/executive accountability for direction and oversight.

items.stem: The core aim of benefits realization in enterprise IT governance is to:

options.text: Ensure IT investments deliver their intended business value
options.rationale: Correct: benefits realization tracks that investments achieve expected value.

options.text: Maximize the number of projects started
options.rationale: Starting projects is not the same as realizing benefits.

options.text: Minimize all IT spending to zero
options.rationale: Governance balances value and cost, not zero spend.
Technology serves strategy; it does not replace it.

items.explanation: Correct: benefits realization tracks that investments achieve expected value.

items.stem: Select TWO components of an effective IT risk optimization approach.

options.text: Identifying and assessing IT-related risks against risk appetite
options.rationale: Correct: risk optimization starts with identifying and assessing risk vs appetite.

options.text: Defining risk responses and monitoring residual risk
options.rationale: Correct: responses and ongoing monitoring are essential to optimization.

options.text: Ignoring risk because controls are expensive
options.rationale: Ignoring risk is the opposite of optimization.

options.text: Transferring every risk regardless of cost-benefit
options.rationale: Blanket transfer ignores cost-benefit and appetite.

options.text: Documenting risks but never acting on them
options.rationale: Documentation without response is not optimization.

items.explanation: Correct: risk optimization starts with identifying and assessing risk vs appetite.
